keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Costs vary enormously depending on whether the boat is stationary in a marina, coastal cruising, or blue-water ocean passage-making — each has different fuel, maintenance, and provisioning costs.
Whether this is for a solo sailor, a couple, or a family with children changes boat size requirements, insurance, schooling, and total monthly spend significantly.
Geographic region (e.g., U.S. East Coast, Caribbean, Mediterranean, Pacific) dramatically affects marina fees, taxes, provisioning costs, and healthcare access.
Whether the person already owns a boat, is budgeting to buy one, or has a fixed monthly budget ceiling shapes which cost categories to prioritize in the research.
Knowing whether this research is for a go/no-go decision, building a detailed budget spreadsheet, or writing content for others determines how deep and structured the output needs to be.
Some people want a frugal, minimalist live-aboard life; others want comfort and reliability. This changes which cost benchmarks are relevant (e.g., budget cruiser vs. well-equipped offshore yacht).
The desired output format — a written report, a spreadsheet, a list of sources to read, or a side-by-side comparison — determines how the research should be structured and delivered.

gold.taskDescription: Gather and organize information about the real costs involved in living full-time on a sailboat.

questions.title: Will the boat be docked, coastal, or ocean-passage sailing?
questions.description: Identify the intended sailing lifestyle — permanently marina-based, coastal cruising within a region, or long-distance blue-water passage-making — as this is the single biggest driver of ongoing costs.

questions.title: How many people will be living aboard full-time?
questions.description: Clarify the crew size — solo, couple, or family with children — to ensure the research covers the right boat size, insurance tier, and per-person cost benchmarks.

questions.title: Which geographic region or sailing area is the focus?
questions.description: Pin down the primary region (e.g., U.S. East Coast, Caribbean, Mediterranean) since marina fees, healthcare costs, and provisioning prices differ drastically by location.

questions.title: Do you already own a boat, or is purchase cost included?
questions.description: Determine whether the research should cover one-time acquisition and refit costs alongside ongoing monthly expenses, or focus solely on the live-aboard operating budget.

questions.title: Is this for a personal go/no-go decision or something else?
questions.description: Understand the end purpose — personal financial planning, writing an article, advising someone else, etc. — so the depth, tone, and structure of the research match the actual need.

questions.title: Are you aiming for a frugal setup or a comfortable, well-equipped one?
questions.description: Establish the comfort and reliability tier the user has in mind, since a budget live-aboard and a fully outfitted offshore yacht can differ by 5x or more in monthly running costs.

questions.title: What format do you want the final research delivered in?
questions.description: Confirm the desired deliverable — a written summary, a categorized spreadsheet, a reading list, or a side-by-side cost comparison — so the output is immediately usable.
